title: Binary Prefixes Divisible by 5
description: You are given a binary array `nums` containing only `0`s and `1`s. Define `x_i` as the integer whose binary representation is the subarray `nums[0..i]` from most significant bit to least significant bit. Return a boolean array `answer` of the same length where `answer[i]` is `true` if `x_i` is divisible by `5`, and `false` otherwise.
hints: Appending a bit `b` to a binary number `x` shifts it left by 1 and ORs in `b`: `x_new = (x << 1) | b`.
Track only `x % 5` at each step using `rem = ((rem << 1) | bit) % 5` to avoid integer overflow.

examples.explanation: The prefixes represent 0, 1, and 3 in decimal; only 0 is divisible by 5.
The prefixes represent 1, 3, and 7; none is divisible by 5.
The prefixes represent 1, 2, 5, 10, and 21; 5 and 10 are divisible by 5.
